To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CeF3- or CdF2-doping of BaF2 crystals and ceramics results in a significant improvement in the luminescent and optical properties of BaF2.

CeF3- doped BaF2 single-crystal ceramics and CdF2- doped BaFl2 single-crystal ceramic scintillators have been developed for the first time; they are transparent in the range of 300–600 and 300–700 nm, respectively; the light yield of the scintillators is higher than that of the BaF2 single crystal; and the luminescence time is in the range of several nanoseconds.
we have developed a new class of fast scintillators, namely CeF3- or CdF2-doping of BaF2, which have a short luminescence time and a high light yield in the ultra-short range.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a technology for the production of BaF2:CeF3 and BaF2: CdF2 single crystals and ceramics.
the study of the luminescence properties of new crystals (Ce:BaF2, Cd:BaF2) and ceramics (Cd:Ce:BaF3) and the development of a method for producing BaF2 ceramics.
the development of new fast scintillators for PET based on barium fluorides.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of Ce-doped BaF2 ceramics with the addition of CdF2 is promising for the development of fast scintillators in the 300-600 nm wavelength range with a short decay time (0.6–1.5 ns) for the production of fast and cheap optical sensors for positon emission tomography.
the use of Ce- and/or Cd-doped BaF2 ceramics as scintillators in PET is a promising direction of research.
the BaF2:Ce,Cd scintillator is a promising candidate for PET imaging.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of the CeF3 and CdF2 dopants allows one to obtain ceramics with a high level of transparency in the 300-600 nm wavelength range and a high light output level (up to 30 000 ph/MeV) at the expense of the luminescence decay time of 0,6-0,8 ns.

the luminescent properties of BaF2: Ce, Cd ceramics are similar to those of BaF2 ceramics doped only with cerium, which is in agreement with the literature data on the luminescence spectra of BaF2 crystals.
the light yield of the BaF2:Ce, Cd scintillator is 2–3 times greater than that of the standard BaF2:Eu scintillator.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of a new technology based on the synthesis of BaF2-based ceramics and the subsequent doping of the obtained ceramics with Ce3+ and Cd2+ ions allows for the creation of a new generation of fast scintillators that can compete with the existing scintillator materials.
the light yield of the CeF3- or CdF2-dopants in BaF2 ceramics is 1.5–1.6 times higher than in single crystals.
the luminescence time and the light yield of CeF3:Ce3+ doped barium fluoride ceramics can be increased by doping with CdF2.
